title: Storing phone numbers
context: Should a phone number be stored as INT or as VARCHAR?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): MySQL questions
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Use VARCHAR. Phone numbers are identifiers, not quantities: they can start with zero, include a plus sign, spaces or country codes, and need no arithmetic. An INT drops leading zeros and overflows for long international numbers. Store the normalised form, such as E.164 with a plus sign, in a VARCHAR, and add a unique index if each number must belong to one user.

points.title: Identifiers are text
points.why: Leading zeros and symbols are lost in an INT, so the value changes.

points.title: Normalise and index
points.why: Store E.164 format and index the column when it must be unique.
